title: Lodestar POC kickoff play notes
overview: Working notes from the Lodestar Analytics POC kickoff. Customer wants to validate Redwood inference for a semi-real-time summarization pipeline across mixed short and long inputs. This doc captures objectives, measurable acceptance criteria, immediate risks, and the sprint play to reach an initial production-equivalent demo in six weeks.
goals: Prove end-to-end integration: customer app -> Redwood Hosted API -> response persisted to event store
Demonstrate latency and cost profile for 95% of queries under realistic load
Surface edge cases for long-document summarization and rollout a mitigation plan
Deliver an internal tech-runbook and a customer-facing demo script
success_criteria: Functional: Summaries for a canonical 10k-token doc set match customer quality baseline on human eval > 75%
Latency: P95 end-to-end generation (including network) < 800ms for <=1024-token requests and < 2.5s for 10k-token workloads when using prefix caching
Throughput: Dedicated test harness can sustain 60 concurrent users with 200 RPS aggregate without error spikes
Cost: Estimated token cost at scale within 30% of the customer's target TCO for month-1 traffic profile
Reliability: No data exfiltration findings from security scan, and audit log events available for all API calls
Operational: Canary rollouts configured with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant on latency or error threshold breach
kickoff_agenda: 15:00 - Proposed technical architecture and data flow (15m)
40:00 - Security & compliance checklist and data residency (10m)
60:00 - Immediate blockers, owners, and next steps (10m)
risks_and_mitigations: Long-doc inference cost blowout: mitigate with prefix/KV caching + demo quantized model to show cost delta
Customer network egress constraints: propose in-VPC private deployment for phase 2 and use token-redaction for demo data
Latency variability on peak load: set up auto-burst policy and throttled client demo harness to avoid SLO breaches
Quality regressions between model variants: reserve an evaluation set and automated eval checks on every model swap
SRE ramp: on-call coverage unclear for weekend demo run — assign SRE buddy and run a dry-fire test
assumptions: Customer will provide a representative sample corpus (10-15 docs) and a small set of gold summaries within 5 business days
We have permission to use subset of production traffic to seed load tests under NDA
Customer accepts a staged plan: hosted API demo first, private deployment for compliance-sensitive workloads later
Access to the customer's telemetry endpoint for latency probes will be provisioned by week 2

technical_scope:
Minimum viable proof-of-value architecture:
- Ingest: HTTPS webhook from customer app to Redwood API
- Serving: Redwood Hosted API using quantized 8-bit variant for demos; option to switch to full-precision in Dedicated pool
- Caching: prefix/KV cache enabled for repeated document fragments
- Observability: per-request token cost, latency tracing, and model version tags to Splunk/Datadog
- Security: TLS, request-level audit logs, and token redaction for pii fields
acceptance_test_plan: Run canonical dataset through pipeline; collect human eval scores and compare to baseline
Synthetic load test: ramp to 200 RPS for 10 minutes while monitoring p95 latency and error rate
Failover test: trigger model variant fallback and validate continuity of responses within SLA
Security checklist: run static scan and ensure audit log completeness for demo requests
Cost estimate validation: run representative 100k token batch and reconcile invoice estimator against expected unit costs
